# Introduction

`clevRact` (*clonal evolution in R analysing conserved trajectories*) provides
an interactive Shiny application for exploratory analysis of conserved patterns
in cohorts of patient-specific tumor phylogenies. The application is designed
around a left-to-right workflow: raw input data are loaded or created first,
then transformed into a processed representation, summarized with cohort
statistics, analysed for recurrent linear signatures, and finally used to
approximate conserved branching trajectories.

# Installation and launching the app

The development repository is <https://github.com/MalteNick/clevRact>. Once the
package is available through Bioconductor, it can be installed with:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("clevRact")
```

The package is intended for interactive use. The main entry point returns a
Shiny application object without starting a server:

```{r create-app}
library(clevRact)
app <- clevRactApp()
class(app)
```

Start the application from an interactive R session:

```{r launch-app, eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp(app)
```

For an editor or remote session where the browser is opened separately, choose a
local address and port:

```{r launch-localhost, eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp(app, host = "127.0.0.1", port = 3838, launch.browser = FALSE)
```

Then open `http://127.0.0.1:3838` in a browser. Stop the application with Escape
in the R console or Ctrl+C in a terminal.

The following sections follow the five tabs of the application from left to
right. The vignette does not launch the Shiny interface during package checks.
Instead, it documents the expected input format and the main analysis steps so
that the workflow can be reproduced with the example files installed in the
package.

# Example input file

`clevRact` installs `synthetic_10_patients.csv` in `inst/extdata`. This
artificial cohort can be uploaded directly in the application and provides
coordinates for automatic annotation. The worked example below describes its
construction and expected results.

```{r example-files}
example_files <- list.files(
    system.file("extdata", package = "clevRact"),
    pattern = "[.]csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
)
basename(example_files)
```

# Input data format

Input files are semicolon-separated CSV files. Each row describes one variant in
one clone of a patient-specific tumor tree. The semicolon separator is used so
that commas can remain part of cell values when needed.

```{r inspect-example}
example_input_file <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "synthetic_10_patients.csv",
    package = "clevRact"
)

example_input <- utils::read.csv(example_input_file, sep = ";", nrows = 3)
example_input
```

The required columns are:

* `Patient.ID`: patient identifier.
* `Variant`: variant label or identifier.
* `Clone`: positive integer identifying the clone.
* `Parent`: parent clone identifier. The value `0` represents the normal-cell
    root.
* `Variant.Type`: one of `CNV_del`, `CNV_dup`, `CNV_loh`, `SNV/INDEL`, or
    `NA`.
* `Chromosome`: chromosome `1`--`22`, `X`, `Y`, or `NA`.
* `Start` and `End`: genomic positions or `NA`.

Optional time-point columns can be added as `T1`, `T2`, and so on. A value of
`TRUE` means that a clone is observed at this time point; `FALSE` means that it
is not observed. The `Clone` and `Parent` columns must describe a valid rooted
tree for each patient. All rows belonging to one clone must have the same
parent. The root has identifier `0` and carries no variant row.

Separate rows can carry the same `Variant` label. They remain distinct event
occurrences, including when they belong to the same clone. For example, two
NOTCH1 mutations can share the label `NOTCH1` without being merged into one
event. Choosing an enumeration option during preprocessing changes those labels
and therefore changes which events can match across patients.

# App workflow

## Input data

The *Input Data* tab is used to create, load, inspect, and edit raw cohort data.
Users can start from a blank dataset or load an existing CSV file. Patients and
variants can be added or removed, the number of time points can be changed, and
the edited cohort can be exported again as a CSV file.

For visual inspection, the app uses `clevRvis` to display patient-specific tumor
trees as shark and dolphin plots. If only Boolean time-point observations are
available, `clevRact` creates compatible cancer-cell-fraction-like values for
visualization. These values are used for plotting and are not interpreted as
measured biological quantities.

## Processed data

The *Processed Data* tab transforms the raw table into the representation used
for signature and trajectory computation. This step is intentionally separate
from data input, because preprocessing choices can change the level of detail at
which variants are analysed. After changing the raw data or these settings,
click *Generate Processed Data* again.

Important settings include:

* generating variant labels from supplied labels or from GRCh37/GRCh38 genomic
    positions;
* representing SNVs/INDELs by gene or by exact chromosome-position labels;
* representing CNVs by chromosome, chromosome arm, or exact interval;
* retaining or enumerating repeated variant labels;
* summarizing same-type CNVs occurring in the same clone and chromosome.

Set *Generate variant labels? = No* to keep the supplied `Variant` identifiers.
Automatic GRCh37 or GRCh38 encoding uses the genomic coordinates and variant
types in the input. Select the reference assembly matching the input
coordinates. The packaged gene mappings include chromosome X and Y.

For analyses of repeated events, *No differentiation* retains shared labels.
Enumeration distinguishes occurrences in their identifiers and is useful when
that distinction is intended.

For regional CNV analysis, select *Use exact CNVs*, *No differentiation*, and
*Summarize same-type CNVs within same clone and chromosome? = No*. Exact CNV
identifiers retain the alteration type, chromosome and interval boundaries;
chromosome-level labels discard the boundaries needed for regional analysis.

During preprocessing, rows that cannot be represented consistently under the
selected settings may be excluded. The app reports these changes so that users
can compare the processed data with the original input.

## Data statistics

The *Data Statistics* tab summarizes the processed cohort. These summaries are
useful for biological inspection, but also for judging the computational scale
of later steps. In particular, the number of patients, clones, variants, and
recurrent variant labels directly influences how many candidate signatures and
trajectories can be generated.

The tab reports, among other summaries, patient counts by clone number, patient
counts by variant number, chromosome distributions, variant recurrence across
patients, CNV/SNV proportions, and the most frequent variants.

## Signature computation

An evolutionary signature is a recurrent linear sequence of variants observed in
the processed tumor trees. `clevRact` enumerates possible linear paths through
each patient tree and records in which patients identical variant sequences are
observed. This means that signatures describe conserved orders of events rather
than only sets of co-occurring variants.

The user settings on the left side of the tab determine the actual computation:

* *Minimum number of occurrences* determines the patient support required for
    signatures to appear in the result table.
* *Maximum signature length* controls the longest linear sequence that is
    generated. Increasing this value can quickly enlarge the search space.
* *Allow sequences within clone* controls whether multiple variants assigned to
    the same clone may be ordered within one signature.

The filter controls above the result table are applied after computation. They
are useful for exploration because they do not require recomputing the complete
signature table.

Significance estimation is also separated from enumeration. This allows users to
compare available significance measures without recomputing the candidate
signatures. The app adds relative occurrence and p-value information to the
signature table. The dropdown offers:

* *Uniform label probabilities*: each distinct alteration label in a patient
    receives the same assignment probability under the approximate null model.
* *Multiplicity-adjusted label probabilities*: assignment probabilities are
    additionally multiplied by the numbers of matching event occurrences within
    that patient.

Both methods use an upper-tail Poisson-binomial enrichment probability for the
observed patient support. The default is *Uniform label probabilities*.
Occurrence counts refer to distinct supporting patients; multiple matches in one
patient contribute one supporter. Relative occurrence is conditional on patients
containing the required alteration labels with sufficient multiplicity, rather
than on the complete cohort.

### Optional CNV region analysis

After computing signatures, *Analyze shared CNV regions* replaces exact CNV
labels by alternative regional labels. It partitions each chromosome using the
start positions and the positions immediately after the ends of all exact CNVs
in the processed cohort. The partition is global across those patients and CNV
types. Each regional label retains the type of the source CNV.

For example, two overlapping deletions with different exact identifiers can
support the same regional deletion-to-gene signature. A source CNV spanning
several regions produces alternative regional signatures. These are separate
descriptions of the same event. Original patient trees and original signatures
remain unchanged.

The step uses the complete extracted signature catalogue, including signatures
below the original result-table support threshold. It pools supporting patient
IDs for identical regional signatures, counts each patient once, and applies the
current *Minimum number of occurrences* threshold to the pooled results. This
allows individually rare exact CNVs to contribute to a recurrent region. The
regional table is separate from the original signature table and can be saved
with *Export region signatures*. Source p-values and relative frequencies are
not transferred to the pooled results.

Exact identifiers have a format such as `CNV_del_9_21600000_22050000` and can
also be supplied directly with automatic label generation disabled. Interval
endpoints are inclusive. If no recognizable exact CNV identifiers are present,
the application shows an error notification. In a mixed catalogue, only
recognizable exact CNV labels are regionalized. Chromosome-arm labels alone
cannot supply the missing boundaries.

## Trajectory approximation

The *Trajectory Approximation* tab recombines previously computed linear
signatures into branching structures called trajectories. The trajectory search
uses the current filters from the *Signature Computation* tab, whether or not
the filtered table view is enabled. The signature filters can therefore be used
as a scalability step before the more expensive branching search is started.

The main trajectory settings are:

* *Minimum number of occurrences*: minimum number of patients in which an
    intermediate or completed trajectory must be observed.
* *Number of recombinations*: maximum number of signature-recombination rounds.
    Higher values allow larger branching structures, but increase the number of
    pairwise combinations.
* *Include independent branches through the root?*: enables additional recurrent
    trajectory bases whose branches meet at the variant-free root. It is enabled
    by default. Disabling it leaves ordinary recombination of linear signatures
    available.
* *Allow the same variant to form multiple subclones*: allows the same variant
    label to occur on separate branches, representing parallel occurrence in
    distinct subpopulations.

Independent-root bases are computed directly from the processed cohort and must
meet the trajectory patient-support threshold. They can be found even if no
linear signature passes the filters. The repeated-label option must also be
enabled to find, for example, two parallel NOTCH1 events. Each supporting
patient must contain separate event occurrences in the required branches.

The recombination setting limits subsequent extensions by retained linear
signatures. Independent-root initialization is a separate step, so its number of
branches is not limited to one per recombination round.

During recombination, `clevRact` joins compatible signatures, checks whether the
resulting branching structures can be embedded in the patient trees, and keeps
the patients supporting each candidate trajectory. Because the trajectory search
space grows with the number of filtered signatures, the number of variants per
patient, and the allowed recombination depth, it is often best to start with
strict support and signature filters and then relax them gradually.

Trajectory significance estimation compares observed trajectory support with
topology-aware background counts. The app can also apply the Benjamini-Hochberg
adjustment to the resulting p-values. Trajectory scoring currently uses *Uniform
label probabilities*. Its relative-occurrence denominator also requires the
patient's tree to admit the candidate topology. Save the trajectory table with
*Export Trajectory Data*.

# Worked example: ten synthetic patients

The packaged file `synthetic_10_patients.csv` contains ten artificial patient
histories. It combines exact mutation matches, repeated gene labels, resolved
and unresolved orders, branching structures and overlapping CNVs. All event
placements are synthetic; the coordinates follow GRCh37.

Patients p01--p08 have overlapping chromosome 9 deletions. Patients p01 and p02
share exactly the same deletion boundaries; the other six deletions have unique
boundaries. Patients p09 and p10 instead have a duplication and LOH event with
overlapping intervals. These two events remain distinct CNV types.

Every patient has a NOTCH1 event at the same position and a downstream FBXW7
event at the same position. A second NOTCH1 event is placed as follows:

| Patients | Relationship between the NOTCH1 events |
|:---------|:---------------------------------------|
| p01--p04 | Separate branches descending from the deletion clone |
| p05--p06 | Two successive clones on the same lineage |
| p07--p08 | Two events in one clone, with unresolved order |
| p09--p10 | Separate branches meeting only through the germline root |

The second NOTCH1 position is identical in p01--p08 and differs in p09--p10.
PHF6 events on chromosome X in p03/p04 and DDX3Y events on chromosome Y in
p09/p10 provide additional checks of reference-genome annotation. Two Boolean
observation columns allow inspection of the temporal visualization.

The following code creates the same cohort as the packaged CSV:

```{r synthetic-example}
patients <- sprintf("p%02d", seq_len(10))
deletions <- data.frame(
    start = c(21600000, 21600000, 21700000, 21800000,
                21650000, 21750000, 21680000, 21780000),
    end = c(22050000, 22050000, 22100000, 22200000,
            22150000, 22080000, 22120000, 22180000)
)

example_event <- function(label, clone, parent, type, chromosome,
                            start, end = start) {
    data.frame(
        Variant = label, Clone = clone, Parent = parent,
        Variant.Type = type, Chromosome = chromosome,
        Start = as.integer(start), End = as.integer(end)
    )
}

example_cohort <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(patients), function(i) {
    cnvs <- if (i <= 8) {
        example_event("9p deletion", 1L, 0L, "CNV_del", "9",
                        deletions$start[i], deletions$end[i])
    } else {
        rbind(
            example_event("9p duplication", 1L, 0L, "CNV_dup", "9",
                            23000000, 25000000),
            example_event("9p LOH", 1L, 0L, "CNV_loh", "9",
                            24000000, 26000000)
        )
    }
    first_notch1 <- example_event(
        "NOTCH1_A", 2L, 1L, "SNV/INDEL", "9", 139390656)
    second_notch1 <- example_event(
        if (i <= 8) "NOTCH1_B" else "NOTCH1_C",
        if (i %in% 7:8) 2L else 3L,
        if (i %in% 5:6) 2L else if (i <= 8) 1L else 0L,
        "SNV/INDEL", "9", if (i <= 8) 139397640 else 139399365)
    fbxw7 <- example_event(
        "FBXW7", if (i %in% 7:8) 3L else 4L,
        if (i %in% 5:6) 3L else 2L, "SNV/INDEL", "4", 153245299)
    sex_chromosome <- if (i %in% 3:4) {
        example_event("PHF6", 5L, 2L, "SNV/INDEL", "X", 133507300)
    } else if (i %in% 9:10) {
        example_event("DDX3Y", 5L, 0L, "SNV/INDEL", "Y", 15016050)
    } else {
        NULL
    }
    rows <- rbind(cnvs, first_notch1, second_notch1, fbxw7, sex_chromosome)
    rows$Patient.ID <- patients[i]
    rows$T1 <- rows$Clone <= 2L
    rows$T2 <- TRUE
    rows[, c("Patient.ID", "Variant", "Clone", "Parent", "Variant.Type",
                "Chromosome", "Start", "End", "T1", "T2")]
}))
rownames(example_cohort) <- NULL
head(example_cohort, 8)
table(example_cohort$Patient.ID)
```

To locate the installed example for upload:

```{r locate-synthetic-example}
packaged_example <- system.file(
    "extdata", "synthetic_10_patients.csv", package = "clevRact")
stopifnot(file.exists(packaged_example))
```

Alternatively, write the generated cohort to your R session's temporary folder
and upload the file identified by `example_file`:

```{r write-synthetic-example}
example_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "clevract-example.csv")
utils::write.table(
    example_cohort,
    file = example_file,
    sep = ";",
    row.names = FALSE,
    quote = TRUE,
    na = "NA"
)
```

## Reference settings and expected observations

Load the file in *Input Data*. Inspect the table or switch to the plots to view
individual histories at T1 and T2. In *Processed Data*, select GRCh37 label
generation, gene-level SNV/INDEL summaries, *Use exact CNVs*, *No
differentiation*, and no same-clone CNV summarization. Click *Generate Processed
Data*. The processed cohort contains ten patients and 46 events. PHF6 and DDX3Y
should retain their gene names after annotation.

Compute signatures with minimum occurrences 2 and maximum length 2. Initially
disable sequences within clones. Estimate significance with *Uniform label
probabilities*. The following observations provide checks of the settings:

| Setting or result | Expected patient support |
|:------------------|-------------------------:|
| Gene-level NOTCH1 followed by FBXW7, resolved order | 10 |
| Gene-level NOTCH1 followed by NOTCH1, resolved order | 2 |
| Gene-level NOTCH1 followed by NOTCH1, including within-clone orders | 4 |
| Exact deletion `21600000--22050000` followed by NOTCH1 | 2 |
| Regional deletion `21800000--22050000` followed by NOTCH1 | 8 |
| Two parallel gene-level NOTCH1 events, resolved ancestry | 6 |
| Exact-position `9_139390656` followed by `4_153245299` | 10 |
| Exact-position `9_139390656` followed by `9_139397640`, resolved order | 2 |
| Exact-position `9_139390656` followed by `9_139397640`, within clones | 4 |

Some signatures omit intermediate events. For example, the shared
NOTCH1-to-FBXW7 ordering remains present in p05/p06 even though the second
NOTCH1 event lies between the two selected events.

## P-values, filters and unresolved order

Inspect the support and p-value columns after *Estimate Significance*. Change
the estimation method to *Multiplicity-adjusted label probabilities* and
estimate again to compare the two calculations. Restore *Uniform label
probabilities* before the branching examples.

Use the variant search field to select NOTCH1 or FBXW7 and try the absolute,
relative-occurrence and p-value filters. The relative-occurrence denominator can
differ between signatures, so it is not always the cohort size of ten. Before
trajectory reconstruction, clear the search and set the signature filters to
minimum absolute support 2, minimum relative occurrence 0, and maximum p-value
1. These values also apply when the filtered-table view is disabled.

To test unresolved order, enable sequences within clones and recompute
signatures. The NOTCH1-to-NOTCH1 signature gains p07 and p08, increasing support
from two to four. This adds permitted orderings within their shared clone; it
does not turn their two events into separate branches. Disable this option and
recompute signatures before checking the resolved branching counts below.

## CNV overlap and regional export

Click *Analyze shared CNV regions* after signature computation. The exact
deletion shared by p01/p02 supports a deletion-to-NOTCH1 signature in two
patients. The other six exact deletions are individually below support two, but
their extracted signatures still contribute to regional pooling. The common
interval `21800000--22050000` is followed by NOTCH1 in all eight deletion
patients. Its support is eight, counting each patient once despite two NOTCH1
events per patient.

The interval `24000000--25000000` is covered by both the duplication and LOH in
p09/p10. The regional output retains distinct duplication and LOH signatures,
each supported by two patients. The partition uses inclusive endpoints and does
not merge these alteration types. Export the table with *Export region
signatures*. The original signatures and patient trees remain unchanged.

## Branching and recombination controls

With resolved orders, minimum trajectory support 2, and two recombination
rounds, enable repeated labels in multiple subclones. Enable independent
branches through the root and compute trajectories. The two parallel NOTCH1
events have support six: p01--p04 and p09/p10. Successive events in p05/p06 and
same-clone events in p07/p08 do not support this branching structure.

Disable independent branches and recompute. The two-event root branching
structure is then absent. Ordinary reconstruction can still recover the shared
exact deletion followed by two NOTCH1 branches, with FBXW7 descending from one
NOTCH1 event, in p01/p02. Compare one and two recombination rounds to inspect
how extensions are added to the retained linear basis. Disabling repeated labels
prevents adding repeated-label branches; linear signatures with repeated labels
remain available. Distinct exact-position labels can still form branches.

After computing trajectories, try *Estimate significant trajectories*, both
available p-value-adjustment settings, the result filters and *Export Trajectory
Data*. The regional signature table is exported separately.

## Exact-position and coarser embeddings

To distinguish repeated gene labels from matches of the same mutation position,
change the SNV/INDEL setting to *Use exact SNVs*, regenerate the processed data,
and recompute signatures. The labels `9_139390656` and `4_153245299` identify
the shared NOTCH1 and FBXW7 positions and have ordered support ten. The
`9_139390656` to `9_139397640` signature has support two with resolved order and
four with within-clone orderings enabled.

Under exact-position encoding, the parallel pair `9_139390656` and `9_139397640`
is supported by p01--p04, while the parallel pair `9_139390656` and
`9_139399365` is supported by p09/p10. Their gene-level representation combines
these as two NOTCH1 events in six patients. Exact SNV encoding here means
chromosome and position; reference and alternate alleles are not part of the
automatically generated label. Since the exact-position labels in this example
are unique within each patient, the two p-value methods agree in this encoding.
Allele-specific labels can instead be supplied directly with label generation
disabled.

For comparison, try chromosome-level or chromosome-arm CNV encoding. The eight
deletions then share a coarser identifier, while interval-level refinement
requires returning to exact CNVs. Enumeration can be compared with *No
differentiation* to inspect its effect on repeated labels. Regenerate processed
data and recompute results after each encoding change. Keep unenumerated exact
CNVs for regional postprocessing.

# Practical recommendations

For larger cohorts, the most important practical strategy is to keep the first
search intentionally strict:

1. preprocess the data and inspect the cohort statistics;
2. compute short signatures first;
3. use a minimum occurrence threshold greater than one;
4. filter signatures before trajectory approximation;
5. increase signature length or recombination depth only after checking result
    size and runtime.

This workflow keeps the analysis exploratory while making the growth of the
search space visible to the user.
